title: A login verified against a hash read before set-password could still rotate the session, and its rehash overwrote the new password
resolution: The rotation transaction rereads the principal and refuses the login unless it is enabled and still has the verified hash; tests change the password during the verification, with and without a rehash

title: A login rotated an anonymous session that had expired while the password was verified
resolution: The rotation transaction rereads the session and answers unauthenticated unless it is still live; a test expires it during the verification

title: submitTask checked the role on its run's project only after reading and validating the body, which section 2 allows only for createRun
resolution: A resource-project rule names where its project is; the server checks a path resource's project through authorizeResource before the body, and an HTTP test shows an invalid body does not precede the denial

title: The HTTP schema counts a login password before NFC, so a password set at 1024 characters after NFC can be refused at login in another form
resolution: Coordinator decision (c): the contract keeps Password.maxLength 1024; checkNewPassword also refuses a password whose NFD form exceeds 1024 code points, counted as Ajv counts maxLength, so every equivalent spelling fits at login

title: An unknown login name verified at the current parameters, while a wrong password for a legacy hash cost only its weaker parameters
resolution: A failed verification lasts at least the last measured cost at the current parameters; a test with a costed fake shows equal costs for an unknown name and a current and a legacy hash

title: The request log kept every query parameter, so a password or an unprefixed session or CSRF token in the query was logged
resolution: Routes declare their document's query parameters and the log keeps only those, still redacted; unit and HTTP tests, a route check against the documents, and section 7 says so

title: The secret reader decoded each chunk alone, so a multibyte character split across chunks became replacement characters
resolution: A StringDecoder decodes across chunks; a test splits a line at every byte

title: Ctrl-C in raw mode ended the secret line as if confirmed, so set-password could store the partial password
resolution: Ctrl-C answers a cancelled failure after restoring the terminal mode, and set-password then writes nothing; a unit test and an integration test of hash, audit, and sessions

title: The login throttle let parallel attempts all pass before a failure was recorded, so one client could fill the hash queue and make every login answer 503, and evicting old keys reset a target's counter
resolution: Attempts run one at a time per source address and per login name with the delay between them, an address with 4 attempts pending gets 503 at once, and a full key table delays new keys instead of forgetting live ones; tests of six parallel attempts and of a filled table

title: The raw-mode secret reader stored backspace, Ctrl-U, and escape sequences in the password, ended at Ctrl-D in mid-line, and asked for the password only once
resolution: On a terminal backspace and delete drop a code point, Ctrl-U clears the line, Ctrl-D ends only an empty line as a cancel, other control keys refuse the input, and set-password reads the password twice and requires a match; unit tests for each

title: The spec deltas left out login throttling, session lifetimes, ending sessions on a password change, the deny-alike rule for run resources, and the temporary G2 bridge
resolution: Five requirements with a scenario each, the lifetimes and throttle limits marked provisional and the bridge temporary until item 11; an archive in a scratch copy validates strictly

title: No test tied the password policy maximum to Password.maxLength or showed that a password set at the maximum passes the login schema
resolution: A test reads Password.maxLength from the document, compares it with the policy, and checks the NFC and NFD forms of maximal passwords against the LoginRequest schema

title: The races of a password change during a login rotation were tested only on the in-memory store
resolution: A PostgreSQL test holds the rotation transaction after its principal read while another pool commits a password change, and shows login-failed, the new hash kept, and no logged-in session

title: The PostgreSQL adapter labelled every principal row operator instead of reading its kind column
resolution: The adapter reads the kind column and answers internal for a kind it does not know; a PostgreSQL test inserts an unknown kind

title: control-plane-api.ts imported from the access module twice, and its session port took a parameter that could only be undefined
resolution: The imports are merged, and the port exposes start, which SessionService now offers, for readSession

title: The anonymous session trim deleted the whole excess in one statement, although the design purges in batches
resolution: trimAnonymous takes the purge batch as its limit and deletes the oldest of the excess first; the conformance suite checks the limit on both stores

title: The status line of verification.md still said finding 4 was returned to the coordinator, and task 6.2 was unchecked after pass 1
resolution: The status line names both passes and their outcomes, and tasks 6.2 and 6.3 are checked
